title: Polity syllabus map
scope: GS II bullets 1–9 form the Polity navigation spine. Governance, social justice and international relations remain separate subjects; existing overlapping PYQ themes are shown as related themes. National symbols and political thought remain Prelims context, not invented Mains syllabus bullets.
countNote: Counts are accepted occurrences in the supplied register, not a complete official-paper frequency analysis. A theme may link to multiple topics; do not add topic totals. Mains covers 2013–2025; Prelims covers 2009–2026.

topics.title: Constitution & its foundations
topics.meaning: Origins, rights and limits on change
outline: Begin with constitutional evolution and founding values.
Locate rights, duties and other significant provisions.
Connect amendment powers with constitutional limits.

topics.title: Federalism & local government
outline: Distinguish Union, State and local responsibilities.
Connect the distribution of powers with financial devolution.
Study coordination, disputes and practical limits on decentralisation.

topics.title: Separation of powers
outline: Identify the institutions sharing or checking a power.
Examine the dispute and the mechanism available to resolve it.
Connect institutional independence with accountability.

topics.title: Comparing constitutions
outline: Choose a constitutional feature before comparing countries.
Compare its design, operation and limits.
Explain why a borrowed feature may operate differently in India.

topics.title: Parliament & State legislatures
outline: Start with the structure and representation of each House.
Follow how business, legislation and scrutiny are conducted.
Connect powers and privileges with accountability concerns.

topics.title: Executive, judiciary & groups
outline: Locate the office, ministry, court or association.
Separate structure and appointment from day-to-day functioning.
Connect participation, institutional responsibility and oversight.

topics.title: Elections & representation
outline: Start with electoral representation and its legal framework.
Connect qualifications, disqualifications and election administration.
Distinguish the law from proposals for reform.

topics.title: Constitutional posts & bodies
outline: Identify the constitutional basis of each post or body.
Link appointment and tenure to powers and responsibilities.
Examine independence, checks and practical effectiveness.

topics.title: Statutory & regulatory bodies
topics.meaning: Institutions created and empowered by law
outline: Identify the law and mandate behind each institution.
Distinguish regulatory, statutory and adjudicatory functions.
Connect powers, procedure and accountability.
